title: Artesunate protects against sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy by reducing Akt/FoxO3-mediated apoptosis and inflammation.
authors: Jiang, Xi; Chen, Yankun; Zeng, Yalin; Chen, Yanghao; Yang, Dan; Ling, Zhiyu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究青蒿琥酯通过Akt/FoxO3通路保护脓毒症心肌病，仅涉及蛋白-蛋白信号通路与分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作、TF-DNA结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) is a life-threatening complication of sepsis characterized by acute and reversible myocardial dysfunction, for which effective targeted therapies remain limited. Artesunate (ART), a well-established first-line antimalarial agent, has attracted increasing attention for its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and cytoprotective properties. However, its role in SICM has not been fully elucidated. In this study, a murine SICM model is established using lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to evaluate the effects of ART on animal mortality, cardiac function, histopathology, and biomarkers of myocardial injury. In parallel, the in vitro study is performed using neonatal rat cardiomyocytes and H9c2 cells exposed to LPS in the presence or absence of ART. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses are used to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying ART-mediated cardioprotection. ART administration significantly improves cardiac function, attenuates myocardial injury, alleviates the inflammatory response, and reduces cardiomyocyte apoptosis in LPS-challenged mice. Consistent results are observed in vitro. Integrated multi-omics analyses identify the Akt/FoxO3 signaling pathway as a critical target of ART. ART treatment contributes to increased Akt phosphorylation and subsequent suppression of FoxO3 nuclear translocation and its transcriptional activity. Pharmacological inhibition of Akt using MK2206 or genetic knockdown of FoxO3 by siRNA abolishes the cardioprotective effects of ART. In addition, molecular docking analysis suggests a potential interaction between ART and Akt isoforms. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ART possesses significant cardioprotective effects in experimental SICM through modulation of the Akt/FoxO3 signaling axis, leading to reduced apoptosis and inflammation. ART may serve as a therapeutic candidate for the management of SICM.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症诱导的心肌病（SICM）是脓毒症的一种危及生命的并发症，其特征为急性和可逆性心肌功能障碍，目前有效的靶向治疗手段仍有限。青蒿琥酯（ART）作为一种成熟的一线抗疟药物，因其抗炎、抗氧化和细胞保护特性而日益受到关注。然而，其在SICM中的作用尚未完全阐明。本研究通过脂多糖（LPS）建立小鼠SICM模型，评估ART对动物死亡率、心脏功能、组织病理学及心肌损伤生物标志物的影响。同时，体外研究使用新生大鼠心肌细胞和H9c2细胞，在LPS暴露下，分别在有或无ART的条件下进行。转录组学和代谢组学分析用于阐明ART介导的心脏保护作用的分子机制。ART给药显著改善了LPS攻击小鼠的心脏功能，减轻了心肌损伤，缓解了炎症反应，并减少了心肌细胞凋亡。体外实验结果与此一致。整合多组学分析确定Akt/FoxO3信号通路为ART的关键靶点。ART治疗促进了Akt磷酸化增加，进而抑制FoxO3核转位及其转录活性。使用MK2206对Akt进行药理学抑制或通过siRNA对FoxO3进行基因敲低，均消除了ART的心脏保护作用。此外，分子对接分析提示ART与Akt亚型之间存在潜在相互作用。综上所述，这些发现表明ART通过调节Akt/FoxO3信号轴，在实验性SICM中发挥显著的心脏保护作用，导致凋亡和炎症减少。ART可能作为SICM治疗的一种候选药物。
